label: <DEL> step in long sequences (content-modulated)
explanation: Fires mainly on the <DEL> step (80% of activation mass; 9.8% of <DEL> steps active). Rate rises steeply with L: near zero for L<=5, about 5% of steps at t=8-9, and the share of mass is largest for L=9. The rest is weaker firing in the last 1-2 original tokens just before <DEL> and on the first copy output (recall_idx 0-1). It never fires at t<3 and almost never late in the copy phase. Which <DEL> steps fire depends on sequence content: the rate is higher when the original contains several of d/f/c/x/3/r, and higher still when the first token (the next one to output) is w/g/2/k/b. These cues together give about 0.72 precision but low recall. The content dependence looks distributed, so no single clean predicate captures it. Best predicate: dev F1 0.39, mass recall 0.67. Plain <DEL> & L>=7 has mass recall 0.76 but precision 0.18.
